title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the setup on p.66. There K ⊂ ℂ is a subfield, ideally of finite type over ℚ, and X is a K-scheme of finite type, viewed as the space X(ℂ) with extra algebraic structure.

(4) There is a functor Π₁(X) → Π̂₁(X) from the topological fundamental groupoid of X(ℂ) to its profinite completion. Both groupoids have every point of X(ℂ) as a base point, and the functor is the identity on objects.

(5) On automorphism groups at a point x it gives π₁(X,x) → π̂₁(X_sch,x). Here Grothendieck notes that the profinite groupoid can be defined purely in terms of the ℂ-scheme.

(6) The Riemann existence theorem (SGA1 XII) then identifies the étale fundamental group π₁(X_sch,x) with the profinite completion of the topological π₁(X,x).

(5') For two points x, y the set Hom_{Π₁}(x,y) of homotopy classes of paths is a bitorsor under (π₁(X,y), π₁(X,x)). Hom_{Π̂₁}(x,y) is identified with the profinite bitorsor under (π̂₁(X,y), π̂₁(X,x)) obtained by extending the structure groups along the two completion maps. The proviso is that the homomorphisms satisfy the compatibility needed for extending a bitorsor to make sense. The left margin spells out this general construction: given G → G', H → H' and a (G,H)-bitorsor P, one forms G' ∧^G P ∧^H H', with a morphism (G,H) → (G',H'). The extension is well defined when the two maps are compatible with the identification of H with G that P induces by conjugation; for profinite completion this holds automatically by functoriality. A second margin note says paths are therefore identified with profinite paths, the map (5') being 'injective'.

The page then introduces the automorphism group Aut_{K-cat}(ℂ) of ℂ over K (the symbol is ambiguous; the next page calls it Γ). The next page uses it to act on the set X(ℂ) and on the groupoid Π̂₁(X), which is legitimate because Π̂₁ is purely algebraic. It then restricts to the sub-groupoid on the K̄-points, where the action factors through Gal(K̄/K).

Purpose: this is the foundational setup for the Galois action on profinite fundamental groupoids of moduli spaces (Teichmüller tower), with many base points and with 'topological' paths sitting inside 'profinite' ones. This is the framework of the Esquisse and later of Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld and Nakamura.
errors: The margin remark that Hom_{Π₁}(x,y) → Hom_{Π̂₁}(x,y) is injective holds only when π₁(X,x) is residually finite. That is true for curves and many moduli spaces (surface groups, free groups, mapping class groups). It fails for general complex algebraic varieties: Toledo constructed smooth projective varieties with non-residually-finite π₁. So 'on identifiera' is legitimate in the curve/Teichmüller context but not for arbitrary X of finite type over K, which is the generality p.66 announces.

Minor: the equation numbering is duplicated ((5) is used twice and (6) recurs on the next page), and the bitorsor-extension condition is left vague ('compte tenu d'homomorphismes satisfaisant la condition requise').

ideas.what: Comparison functor from the topological fundamental groupoid of X(ℂ) (all points as base points) to the profinite/étale fundamental groupoid, bijective on objects.
ideas.modern_name: Betti-to-étale comparison of fundamental groupoids; profinite completion of the fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 XII, Riemann existence theorem); groupoid formulation by Grothendieck and later Deligne
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XII (groups); Esquisse d'un programme (groupoids with many base points)

ideas.what: Path sets Hom(x,y) as bitorsors, and the profinite path set as extension of structure groups of the topological bitorsor.
ideas.modern_name: Bitorsors and change of structure groups (contracted product G'∧^G P∧^H H')
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor language is in Giraud 1971, which grew out of Grothendieck's program; not sure it appears in a Grothendieck-authored text

ideas.what: Action of Aut(ℂ/K) (not only Gal(K̄/K)) on X(ℂ) and on the profinite fundamental groupoid with all complex points as base points; restriction to K̄-points, where the action factors through Gal(K̄/K).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale fundamental groupoids; outer Galois representation with tangential/rational base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Deligne 1989 (fundamental group of P¹ minus three points); Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Galois action on the Teichmüller tower

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational setup: the comparison of topological and profinite groupoids, bitorsor extension, and the Aut(ℂ/K) action. All of it is in SGA1, Giraud or the Esquisse. Letting the huge group Aut(ℂ/K) act on the groupoid over all complex points before restricting to K̄-points is a mildly characteristic formulation, but not new.
transcription_corrections: The final displayed symbol '(5) Π_K = Π_K = Aut_{K-cat}(ℂ)' is most likely Grothendieck's Γ (the group called Γ on the next page), with a struck-out subscript K: read 'Γ_K = Aut_{K-cat}(ℂ)', not Π.
In the profinite bitorsor line, 'torseur profini sous (π̂₁(X,y), π̂₁(X,x))' should read 'bitorseur profini', with y on the left and x on the right, matching the source/target convention for Hom(x,y).
Left top margin likely reads: 'On identifiera donc les éléments de Hom_{Π₁}(x,y) à des éléments de Hom_{Π̂₁}(x,y), via l'application (5') qui est injective'.
'De même[?]' at the start of (5') plausibly reads 'De même, pour x, y ∈ X, l'application'.
